diagnostic_evidence.tag: thm: representation of the specular directional derivative

issues.failure_explanation: The 'only if' direction claims that existence of the specular directional derivative forces existence of the one-sided derivatives. Counterexample: X=R, f(t)=|t|(1.5+0.5 sin(log|t|)), f(0)=0. Then f(0)-f(-h)=-(f(h)-f(0)), so the two arctangents cancel exactly and f^sd(0)=0 exists, but the right derivative does not exist. The proof of (H1) derives inequalities (5) and (6) by applying tan to 2arctan((c∓h)/||v||)∓π/2. This is monotone-valid only when the argument lies in (-π/2,π/2), i.e. c-h>0 for (5) and c+h<0 for (6). These cannot both hold, so the liminf/limsup contradiction is invalid.

issues.failure_explanation: The condition |<φ,y>|=||y||_Y for all y∈Y makes φ injective, because φ(y)=0 forces y=0. Hence dim Y ≤ 1. The theorem is presented as a Mean Value Theorem for maps between general normed spaces, but its hypothesis can only hold when Y is (isometric to) R. No genuinely vector-valued case is covered. The proof also writes w=v-u∈Ω, which need not hold.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: However, such representation may not hold for specular directional derivatives because of the nonlinearity.

issues.failure_explanation: The convergence theory requires E[∇^s f_ξ(x)|x_k]=∇^s f(x_k) for f=(1/m)Σ f_j. The specular gradient is nonlinear in f; for example, specular derivatives of sums obey only inequalities. With uniform sampling, E[∇^s f_ξ]=(1/m)Σ∇^s f_j, which in general differs from ∇^s f. At nondifferentiable points of several components this fails, e.g. f_1=|x|, f_2=|x-1|-type kinks coinciding. No sampling scheme or verification is given for which the condition holds, including for the Elastic Net experiments.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either assume and justify (e.g. smooth components or separable structure) that the sampled specular gradient is unbiased for ∇^s f, or restate the guarantee for sampling of subgradients with a proven unbiasedness property.
issues.overall_effect: The convergence theorem for S-SPEG is conditional on an assumption that the implemented algorithm is not shown to satisfy. The claim that the stochastic specular gradient method converges is unsupported for the algorithm actually run.
issues.title: S-SPEG samples a uniform component, but unbiasedness for the nonlinear specular gradient is not justified
issues.why_classification: A restricted-class or assumption-based fix leaves a recognisably comparable result, but the guarantee for the stated algorithm must be weakened.

issues.failure_explanation: Hypothesis (H3) is Σt_k=∞, while h_k=t_k/||∇^s f(x_k)||. Σh_ℓ=∞ needs the gradients ||∇^s f(x_ℓ)|| to be bounded, which is neither assumed nor shown. The stochastic theorem adds a boundedness assumption (H5) for this purpose, but the deterministic theorem does not. Boundedness could be obtained from the boundedness of {x_k} (proved later) and local boundedness of subdifferentials of finite convex functions, but the proof neither orders nor invokes this.

issues.failure_explanation: Here h_ℓ=t_ℓ/||∇^s f_{ξ_ℓ}(x_ℓ)|| depends on the sampled index ξ_ℓ. Therefore E[h_ℓ ∇^s f_ξ | x_ℓ] ≠ h_ℓ E[∇^s f_ξ | x_ℓ].
